title: Why Do Some Memories Survive Dementia?

sentences.en: There was this story that my dad always told about how he fell in love with my mother.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸总是讲这样一个故事，关于他是怎么爱上我妈妈的。

sentences.en: Both of them were living in Europe.
sentences.zh: 他们俩当时都住在欧洲。

sentences.en: It was 1956.
My dad was a student and he had become so passionate about the student uprising in Hungary that he decided to spend his Christmas break assisting the revolution.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸当时是个学生，他对匈牙利的学生起义满腔热情，决定把圣诞假期用来支援这场革命。

sentences.en: So he and a friend made plans to travel down to the border of Hungary and Austria.
sentences.zh: 于是他和一位朋友计划前往匈牙利和奥地利边境。

sentences.en: My mom, who was at that point an acquaintance, tagged along.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈当时只是个熟人，也跟着去了。

sentences.en: But when they got there, she stayed behind and they crossed the border into Hungary.
sentences.zh: 但当他们到达那里时，她留在了后面，而他们越过边境去了匈牙利。

sentences.en: It wasn't long before they encountered a row of Soviet tanks, at which point they decided their work here was done and retreated.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，他们就遇到了一排苏联坦克，于是他们觉得这里的工作已经完成，便撤退了。

sentences.en: Instead, they decided to leave the Hungarians to their own devices and spend the rest of their winter break skiing.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们决定让匈牙利人自行其是，把剩下的寒假时间用来滑雪。

sentences.en: Now, my dad had never been on skis.
sentences.zh: 然而，我爸爸以前从来没滑过雪。

sentences.en: And this is sort of characteristic that the way he approached it was essentially to get on a ski lift to the top of an Alp,
sentences.zh: 他的行事风格很有特点，基本上就是坐着滑雪缆车直接上到阿尔卑斯山顶，

sentences.en: where I guess he imagined that he was going to learn how to ski by skiing down it.
sentences.zh: 我想象他当时大概觉得只要从山顶滑下来就能学会滑雪吧。

sentences.en: And almost immediately dislocated his shoulder and someone called a medic.
sentences.zh: 结果几乎立刻就脱臼了，有人叫了医务人员。

sentences.en: And in preparation for resetting the shoulder, the medic handed my mother a rag soaked in chloroform and told her to hold it over his mouth, which she did.
sentences.zh: 为了帮他复位肩膀，医务人员递给我妈妈一块浸了氯仿的抹布，让她捂住他的嘴，她照做了。

sentences.en: And the way my dad always told this story, he would say, And I woke up married.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸每次讲到这个故事都会说：“然后我醒来时就已经结婚了。”

sentences.en: That was a story that my dad would tell even after his brain injury and dementia had really scrambled many of his memories.
sentences.zh: 即使是在他的脑损伤和痴呆症严重扰乱了许多记忆之后，我爸爸依然会讲这个故事。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams, and this is The Daily on Sunday.
sentences.zh: 这里是《纽约时报》，我是蕾切尔·艾布拉姆斯，这里是周末版每日播客。

sentences.en: Over the course of a few years, Times reporter Ellen Berry watched as her father's memories slipped away to dementia.
sentences.zh: 在几年的时间里，《纽约时报》记者埃伦·贝瑞眼看着父亲的记忆被痴呆症一点点剥夺。

sentences.en: It was the kind of painful experience that a lot of families suffer through, often in isolation.
sentences.zh: 这是一种许多家庭都经历过的痛苦体验，而且往往是在孤立无援中承受。

sentences.en: Today, Ellen recounts her journey with her father and how years after his death, one neuroscientist helped to explain to her
sentences.zh: 今天，埃伦讲述了她与父亲的这段历程，以及在他去世多年后，一位神经科学家如何帮助她解释了

sentences.en: what had happened to him and what her family had gone through.
sentences.zh: 他身上发生了什么，以及她的家庭经历了什么。

sentences.en: It's Sunday, July 26th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月26日，星期日。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜洛。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的“连线”字谜。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我也喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天负责创作“拼字蜂”和“字母包”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做色彩联觉的现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时会看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像刚才你们听到声音的这些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com 斜杠 games，今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.en: Ellen Berry, welcome to the Sunday Daily.
sentences.zh: 埃伦·贝瑞，欢迎来到周末每日播客。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Ellen, you were a foreign correspondent for many years.
sentences.zh: 埃伦，你当过多年的外国常驻记者。

sentences.en: You lived in Moscow, Delhi, London.
sentences.zh: 你住过莫斯科、德里、伦敦。

sentences.en: And recently, you wrote very movingly about your father and his illness and how it affected your family,
sentences.zh: 最近，你写了一篇非常感人的文章，关于你的父亲、他的病情以及这如何影响了你的家庭，

sentences.en: who, if I understand correctly, you moved back to the United States to be closer to.
sentences.zh: 如果我没理解错的话，你搬回美国是为了离他们更近一些。

sentences.en: I want to start by having you describe what specifically prompted that move and how your father's health deteriorated from there.
sentences.zh: 我想先请你描述一下，究竟是什么促成了这次搬迁，以及你父亲的健康状况从那时起是如何恶化的。

sentences.en: We had been in India for four years.
sentences.zh: 我们在印度待了四年。

sentences.en: And in India, you realize that almost everyone lives in a joint family, like a multi-generational family.
sentences.zh: 在印度，你会意识到几乎每个人都生活在联合家庭中，也就是多代同堂的家庭。

sentences.en: I really began to admire this arrangement.
sentences.zh: 我真的开始欣赏这种生活方式。

sentences.en: And my parents were in their late 80s.
sentences.zh: 我父母当时快九十岁了。

sentences.en: They'd spent their lives in the Foreign Service moving every few years.
sentences.zh: 他们一生都在外交部门工作，每隔几年就要搬一次家。

sentences.en: At the time, though, they were in a house in D.C., retired.
sentences.zh: 不过当时，他们退休后住在华盛顿的一所房子里。

sentences.en: And we were looking for a way for them to make a transition into a new arrangement.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在寻找一种方法，让他们能够过渡到一个新的生活安排中。

sentences.en: So we came up with this plan to buy a two-family house.
sentences.zh: 于是我们制定了这个计划，买下一栋双拼房。

sentences.en: And the idea was that they would have some autonomy, live downstairs.
sentences.zh: 想法是他们可以保持一些自主性，住在楼下。

sentences.en: My kids could have a period of time living with them.
sentences.zh: 我的孩子可以有一段时间和他们住在一起。

sentences.en: I sort of knew it was now or never because of their age.
sentences.zh: 考虑到他们的年龄，我隐约觉得机不可失，失不再来。

sentences.en: And so we did it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们就这么做了。

sentences.en: So one week before the movers were supposed to come, my dad had a fall.
sentences.zh: 就在搬家公司要来的前一周，我爸爸摔了一跤。

sentences.en: He fell hard.
sentences.zh: 他摔得很重。

sentences.en: He hit his head on the floor.
sentences.zh: 他的头部撞到了地板上。

sentences.en: It was a hardwood floor.
sentences.zh: 那是硬木地板。

sentences.en: He lost consciousness.
sentences.zh: 他失去了知觉。

sentences.en: My mom was the only person with him, but she thought it was five minutes.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈是唯一和他在一起的人，但她以为只过了五分钟。

sentences.en: It was obviously an extremely serious head injury.
sentences.zh: 这显然是一次极其严重的头部受伤。

sentences.en: And for a few days, it wasn't clear whether he was going to survive it.
sentences.zh: 在最初的几天里，还不清楚他能不能挺过去。

sentences.en: Once they were able to do a brain scan, they told us that he had a subarachnoid hemorrhage, that he had had a brain bleed.
sentences.zh: 等他们能够做脑部扫描时，告诉我们他有蛛网膜下腔出血，脑部有出血。

sentences.en: I remembered subarachnoid because I used to call it under the spider.
sentences.zh: 我记住了“蛛网膜”，因为我以前管它叫“蜘蛛网下”。

sentences.en: But I remember like two days afterwards when the nurse came in and he asked her for a newspaper and a cup of coffee.
sentences.zh: 但我记得大约两天后，护士进来时，他向她要了一份报纸和一杯咖啡。

sentences.en: And that's how we knew that he was okay.
sentences.zh: 我们就是在那时知道他没事了。

sentences.en: So he was improving, healing?
sentences.zh: 所以他当时在好转，在康复？

sentences.en: Yeah, he was up and about and it seemed like he might be recovering.
sentences.zh: 对，他能下床走动了，看起来好像在康复。

sentences.en: But with time and especially with retrospect,
sentences.zh: 但随着时间推移，尤其是事后回想起来，

sentences.en: it's now clear that this is the beginning of a sort of accelerated vascular dementia that ended up being the cause of his death four and a half years later.
sentences.zh: 现在很清楚，那是某种加速型血管性痴呆的开始，最终导致他在四年半后去世。

sentences.en: After the injury, how was he, like, just in terms of cognitive function, how did the injury affect his thinking, speaking, just sort of everyday living?
sentences.zh: 受伤后，他的情况怎么样，比如说，仅就认知功能而言，这次受伤是如何影响他的思维、说话以及日常生活方式的？

sentences.en: Yeah, so he was in a rehab facility for a few weeks and we were just kind of trying to figure out, like, when would he be okay to come home and what exactly were we dealing with?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他在康复中心呆了几周，我们只是在琢磨，他什么时候可以回家，我们到底要面对什么？

sentences.en: And we couldn't tell.
sentences.zh: 而我们当时还无法确定。

sentences.en: It was right after his injury, so it wasn't clear.
sentences.zh: 那是他受伤后不久，所以还不明确。

sentences.en: But some things began to emerge.
sentences.zh: 但有些迹象开始显现。

sentences.en: He began to have what I would describe as bizarre but very interesting delusions.
sentences.zh: 他开始出现我所说的离奇但非常有趣的妄想。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: Can you give us an example?
sentences.zh: 能给我们举个例子吗？

sentences.en: Okay, so he told us that his roommate at the care facility was smuggling black caviar into the country.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他告诉我们，他在护理中心的室友正在向国内走私黑鱼子酱。

sentences.en: And somehow he believed that he had been wrapped into this scheme.
sentences.zh: 不知怎么的，他坚信自己也被卷入了这个计划。

sentences.en: He also reported to me that the nurses here are all KGB.
sentences.zh: 他还向我报告说这里的护士全都是克格勃。

sentences.en: And I said, how do you know?
sentences.zh: 我说，你怎么知道？

sentences.en: And he said, because they speak perfect English.
sentences.zh: 他说，因为他们说一口流利的英语。

sentences.en: Obviously proof.
sentences.zh: 这显然是证据。

sentences.en: But also, more seriously, he didn't really know where he was.
sentences.zh: 但更严重的是，他根本不知道自己在哪里。

sentences.en: He would try to go into the wrong room.
sentences.zh: 他会试图走进错误的房间。

sentences.en: He didn't know why he was in a rehab facility.
sentences.zh: 他不知道自己为什么会在康复中心。

sentences.en: He didn't understand why he couldn't leave.
sentences.zh: 他不明白自己为什么不能离开。

sentences.en: And he was more than before the injury, he was really impulsive.
sentences.zh: 而且比受伤前更甚，他变得非常冲动。

sentences.en: I think we had the idea that all this confusion was a function of being in the hospital and that once we got him home and settled, that it would resolve.
sentences.zh: 我想我们当时觉得，所有这些混乱都是住院造成的，一旦我们把他接回家安顿好，情况就会解决。

sentences.en: So what did it look like when he got home?
sentences.zh: 那么他回家后是什么情况？

sentences.en: What was that like?
sentences.zh: 那是一种什么样的体验？

sentences.en: Well, I think we felt like we had just reached home base somehow that, you know, now he would sort of come to rest in a place that was comfortable.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我们觉得总算回到了大本营，你知道的，现在他终于可以在一个舒适的地方安顿下来了。

sentences.en: They moved into the downstairs and put up, you know, their art from their house in Washington and really kind of recreated the house that they had just left.
sentences.zh: 他们搬进楼下，挂上了他们在华盛顿家里的艺术品，几乎可以说是重现了他们刚刚离开的那个家。

sentences.en: My mom started gardening and she started cooking for him and they had two poodles.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈开始种花，开始为他做饭，他们还养了两只贵宾犬。

sentences.en: There were aspects in which his life was very similar to the routine he had before his injury.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，他的生活与受伤前的日常非常相似。

sentences.en: So he would get up and commit the first two hours of the day to reading the New York Times, walking the dogs.
sentences.zh: 他会起床，把每天头两个小时用来读《纽约时报》、遛狗。

sentences.en: It seemed like things were kind of normal, but really from early days, we began to notice some behavior changes.
sentences.zh: 事情看起来似乎挺正常的，但实际上从一开始，我们就开始注意到一些行为变化。

sentences.en: Some of them were just absurd and sort of comical.
sentences.zh: 其中有些行为简直荒谬，甚至有点滑稽。

sentences.en: He was really impulsive.
sentences.zh: 他真的非常冲动。

sentences.en: The things he wanted were not all that different from the things he would have wanted in his old life.
sentences.zh: 他想要的东西和他在过去的生活中想要的东西其实差不了多少。

sentences.en: For example, my mom said she wanted a birdbath.
sentences.zh: 比如，我妈妈说她想要一个鸟盆。

sentences.en: Like an actual birdbath to be put outside.
sentences.zh: 就像那种放在室外的真正的鸟盆。

sentences.en: She wanted a birdbath.
sentences.zh: 她想要个鸟盆。

sentences.en: And one day we got a birdbath from China.
sentences.zh: 结果有一天我们收到了一个从中国寄来的鸟盆。

sentences.en: And then the next day we got another birdbath from China.
sentences.zh: 然后第二天我们又收到一个从中国寄来的鸟盆。

sentences.en: And we ended up getting seven birdbaths.
sentences.zh: 最后我们收到了七个鸟盆。

sentences.en: One after the other.
sentences.zh: 一个接一个。

sentences.en: Seven birdbaths.
sentences.zh: 整整七个鸟盆。

sentences.en: Incredibly, in a cascade of deliveries, we returned every single one, I guess, but one.
sentences.zh: 难以置信的是，在快递的狂轰滥炸下，除了一个之外，我想我们把每一个都退了。

sentences.en: We must have kept one.
sentences.zh: 我们肯定留了一个。

sentences.en: And we got a delivery of, I think, four or five laptops.
sentences.zh: 然后我们还收到了大概四五台笔记本电脑的快递。

sentences.en: Four or five laptops.
sentences.zh: 四五台笔记本电脑。

sentences.en: Four or five laptops.
sentences.zh: 四五台笔记本电脑。

sentences.en: We had to return all of those, too.
sentences.zh: 那些我们也全都得退掉。

sentences.en: These are things that presumably your father was ordering online when nobody was looking.
sentences.zh: 这些东西想必都是你父亲趁没人注意时在网上订购的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: At one point, I expressed the desire for a Japanese dwarf maple tree.
sentences.zh: 有一次，我表达了想要一棵日本侏儒枫树的想法。

sentences.en: And one night, he just disappeared.
sentences.zh: 结果有一天晚上，他直接失踪了。

sentences.en: He left the house at like three or four in the morning with the car.
sentences.zh: 他大清早三四点钟开着车离开了家。

sentences.en: And we called the police.
sentences.zh: 我们报了警。

sentences.en: And my husband, I don't really know how, he knew immediately where to look for him.
sentences.zh: 我丈夫，我真不知道他是怎么做到的，立刻就知道去哪里找他。

sentences.en: It was the dead of night.
sentences.zh: 当时正值深夜。

sentences.en: And he drove out to a nursery, which was, I don't know, probably a 25-minute drive.
sentences.zh: 他开车去了一家苗圃，大概要开25分钟的车吧。

sentences.en: And he pulled up outside this nursery.
sentences.zh: 他把车停在那家苗圃外面。

sentences.en: And my dad was there alone, just waiting for the sun to rise.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸就独自在那里，静静地等着太阳升起。

sentences.en: And he had smashed up the car.
sentences.zh: 而且他把车给撞坏了。

sentences.en: It wasn't terrible, but like, he shouldn't have been driving.
sentences.zh: 虽然不是很严重，但是，他当时根本不应该开车。

sentences.en: And then my husband went up to him.
sentences.zh: 然后我丈夫朝他走了过去。

sentences.en: He was sitting outside this nursery.
sentences.zh: 他正坐在那家苗圃外面。

sentences.en: And my dad always knew what to say.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸总是知道该说些什么。

sentences.en: He said, fancy meeting you here.
sentences.zh: 他说：“真巧啊，在这儿碰见你。”

sentences.en: But there was one change in particular that was, for us, very difficult to handle.
sentences.zh: 但有一个变化特别让我们难以应付。

sentences.en: And that was that he thought he was in the wrong place.
sentences.zh: 那就是他觉得自己待错了地方。

sentences.en: And he felt pretty much all the time that he had to leave.
sentences.zh: 他几乎无时无刻都觉得必须离开。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: You know that feeling when you think you might miss your plane?
sentences.zh: 你知道那种觉得自己可能要错过航班的感觉吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 知道。

sentences.en: Kind of restless feeling?
sentences.zh: 一种心神不宁的感觉？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It was like he had that every day.
sentences.zh: 他好像每天都这样。

sentences.en: He would say, well, we have to pack the car to go to drive down to Washington.
sentences.zh: 他会说，好吧，我们得把车收拾好，开车去华盛顿。

sentences.en: Or I have to catch a flight.
sentences.zh: 或者我得去赶飞机。

sentences.en: He said he had to catch a high line to Kiev.
sentences.zh: 他说他得去赶一条通往基辅的高速列车。

sentences.en: He said he had to go to Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: 他说他得去费城。

sentences.en: He said he had to leave the next morning to take a water route to China, which from Massachusetts doesn't make a lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 他说他第二天早上得出发，坐水路去中国，这从马萨诸塞州出发来看完全说不通。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: He said he had to go to Vienna to accept an award, the Votivkirche.
sentences.zh: 他说他得去维也纳领个奖，就在感恩教堂。

sentences.en: He had different ideas about where he was supposed to go, but the feeling was always the same, which is like that feeling of, if we don't get ready,
sentences.zh: 对于自己该去哪儿，他有各种各样的想法，但那种感觉始终如一，就像那种……如果我们不准备好，

sentences.en: we're going to miss our connection.
sentences.zh: 就要赶不上转机了。

sentences.en: I take it that he didn't actually have to go to any of these places, but would he actually try to leave?
sentences.zh: 我的理解是，他其实根本不用去这些地方，但他真的会试图离开吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 会。

sentences.en: What did he do?
sentences.zh: 他会怎么做？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, if he didn't try, it wouldn't have been as much of a problem.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果他没去试，也就不会有这么大麻烦了。

sentences.en: So what he would do is he would pack suitcases.
sentences.zh: 所以他会做的是收拾行李箱。

sentences.en: He would take all the art, all the pictures off the wall and put them in the car.
sentences.zh: 他会把所有的艺术品、墙上的所有画都摘下来塞进车里。

sentences.en: Once he picked up an entire decorated Christmas tree and put it in the car.
sentences.zh: 有一次，他甚至把整棵装饰好的圣诞树搬起来塞进了车里。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And sometimes he would leave.
sentences.zh: 有时他真的会离开。

sentences.en: Sometimes he left on foot.
sentences.zh: 有时他步行离开。

sentences.en: In the early days before we took away the car keys, he left in the car.
sentences.zh: 在我们收走车钥匙之前的早期，他会开车离开。

sentences.en: And so it became a kind of habit in our house that we would catch him as he was trying to leave, and we would try to redirect him.
sentences.zh: 所以这就成了我们家里的一种习惯：每当他试图离开时，我们就会截住他，然后试着引导他改变方向。

sentences.en: We would bring him inside.
sentences.zh: 我们会把他带回屋里。

sentences.en: We would tell him whatever we had to tell him.
sentences.zh: 我们会跟他说任何需要说的话。

sentences.en: Sometimes we would just drive him around so that he had the feeling of movement.
sentences.zh: 有时我们只是开车带他兜风，好让他有那种在移动的感觉。

sentences.en: My husband, God bless him, sometimes took him to Logan Airport and just let him walk into the terminal and then come back to the car.
sentences.zh: 我丈夫——上帝保佑他——有时会带他去洛根机场，让他走进航站楼，然后又回到车上。

sentences.en: Just to be clear, when he is trying to leave and you are interacting with him, are you trying to convince him of where he is, that he doesn't actually have a place to go?
sentences.zh: 说清楚点，当他试图离开而你在和他交流时，你是试图说服他认清自己身在何处，告诉他其实根本没地方可去吗？

sentences.en: Are you trying to reason with him and remind him that this is his home?
sentences.zh: 你是在试图跟他讲道理，提醒他这里是他的家吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I mean, this went on for four years, so all of those things.
sentences.zh: 对，呃，我是说，这种情况持续了四年，所以这些方法都用过。

sentences.en: And when you did try to redirect him in those situations, how would he respond?
sentences.zh: 当你在那种情况下试图引导他时，他会有什么反应？

sentences.en: I mean, he still had the same personality.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他还是老脾气。

sentences.en: He was incredibly stubborn, and he thought we were trying to hoodwink him.
sentences.zh: 他固执得难以置信，还觉得我们是在合伙忽悠他。

sentences.en: We would try to tell him he didn't have to go to the airport, and he didn't believe us.
sentences.zh: 我们会试图告诉他不用去机场，但他根本不信。

sentences.en: There were times when we were really skillful and inventive,
sentences.zh: 有时我们能想出极其巧妙、颇有创意的对策，

sentences.en: and there were times when we were frustrated and desperate and angry that he didn't understand that we had set up this whole arrangement for him.
sentences.zh: 但有时，我们也会感到沮丧、绝望和愤怒，因为他不明白我们为他做了这么周密的安排。

sentences.en: I remember one time my husband, who was the one who did a lot of this redirecting, wrote a note that he stuck on the inside of the door that said,
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次，我丈夫——经常负责这种引导工作的人——写了张便条，贴在门内侧，上面写着：

sentences.en: Bob, you live here.
sentences.zh: 鲍勃，你住在这里。

sentences.en: Don't move.
sentences.zh: 别走。

sentences.en: We love you.
sentences.zh: 我们爱你。

sentences.en: So that when he was leaving, he would somehow be reminded that this is where he belonged.
sentences.zh: 这样当他要离开时，多少能提醒他这里才是他属于的地方。

sentences.en: Did that work?
sentences.zh: 管用吗？

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 其实不管用。

sentences.en: And in the end, we had to get a locksmith to come in and install locks on the insides of the doors just to make sure that he didn't leave during the night.
sentences.zh: 最后，我们不得不请来锁匠，在门内侧安装了锁，以确保他半夜不会溜出去。

sentences.en: Because no matter how many times we told him, he didn't seem to be able to remember that he had decided to move in with us, that we had bought this house together,
sentences.zh: 因为不管我们对他说过多少次，他似乎都记不住自己决定搬来和我们同住、我们一起买下了这栋房子，

sentences.en: and that this is where he was planning to live.
sentences.zh: 以及这就是他计划生活的地方。

sentences.en: So all of that, like, recent stuff that had happened leading up to the move, it was all gone.
sentences.zh: 所以，所有这些搬家前发生的事，那些近期的事，全都没了。

sentences.en: He couldn't access it.
sentences.zh: 他想不起来了。

sentences.en: If he couldn't remember things that were recent, Ellen, were there things that he could remember from farther back?
sentences.zh: 艾伦，如果他记不住近期的事，那他能记住更久远以前的事吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 能。

sentences.en: It seemed like the farther back it was, the better he could remember.
sentences.zh: 似乎时间越久远，他反而记、得越清楚。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: There's a particular night that made me realize this.
sentences.zh: 有个特定的夜晚让我意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: I could hear what was going on in their apartment from my bedroom, and I heard him downstairs, I don't know, it was the middle of the night.
sentences.zh: 我在卧室里能听到他们公寓里的动静，我听到他在楼下，不知道是几点，反正已经是半夜了。

sentences.en: And I went downstairs in my pajamas, and he and my mother were sitting at the kitchen table, and he was crying.
sentences.zh: 我穿着睡衣下楼，发现他和妈妈坐在餐桌旁，他在哭。

sentences.en: And I wasn't used to seeing him cry.
sentences.zh: 我以前从没见他哭过。

sentences.en: He was a very controlled personality, and he was telling a story.
sentences.zh: 他是一个情绪非常克制的人，当时他正在讲一个故事。

sentences.en: She was standing behind him.
sentences.zh: 我妈正站在他身后。

sentences.en: She had her hands on his shoulders, and he was telling this story.
sentences.zh: 双手搭在他的肩膀上，而他在讲着这个故事。

sentences.en: When he was six years old, his family left Pittsburgh, where he had been born.
sentences.zh: 他六岁那年，全家离开了他的出生地匹兹堡。

sentences.en: And they moved to an Air Force base in San Antonio.
sentences.zh: 他们搬到了圣安东尼奥的一个空军基地。

sentences.en: They took a train from Pittsburgh, changed trains in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 他们从匹兹堡坐火车，在芝加哥转车。

sentences.en: He was leaving everything, but he was able to take one pet.
sentences.zh: 他要告别所有的一切，但允许带一只宠物。

sentences.en: The pet was a canary that he was carrying in a cage on the train.
sentences.zh: 那只宠物是一只金丝雀，他把它装在火车的笼子里带着。

sentences.en: And they were in Chicago, in the station, walking to catch their connection to Texas.
sentences.zh: 当他们在芝加哥的车站里走着去转乘去得克萨斯州的列车时，

sentences.en: And the bottom fell out of the cage, and the canary flew out into the station.
sentences.zh: 笼底突然掉了，金丝雀飞进了车站里。

sentences.en: And the canary just goes up into the upper reaches of this station.
sentences.zh: 金丝雀就那样飞到了车站穹顶的高处。

sentences.en: And he had to keep walking with an empty cage and get onto the next train without the canary.
sentences.zh: 他只能提着空笼子继续往前走，在没有金丝雀的情况下上了下一趟火车。

sentences.en: Did you have any idea what had prompted this?
sentences.zh: 你知道是什么触动了他吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不知道。

sentences.en: And sort of beyond that, I knew his life story pretty well.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，我其实挺了解他的人生经历的。

sentences.en: He had written a memoir that he didn't publish, but I had read.
sentences.zh: 他写过一本回忆录，虽然没出版，但我读过。

sentences.en: That story wasn't in it.
sentences.zh: 那个故事并不在里面。

sentences.en: He liked to tell stories.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢讲故事。

sentences.en: That was not a story he had ever told me.
sentences.zh: 但那绝对不是他以前对我说过的故事。

sentences.en: Unlike the KGB nurses, unlike the roommate secretly smuggling caviar, you were able to recognize that this was, in fact, an intact memory.
sentences.zh: 不像克格勃护士，不像偷偷走私鱼子的室友，你当时就能看出这实际上是一段完整的记忆。

sentences.en: Yeah, this was not an anecdote or a story that he was telling us.
sentences.zh: 对，这不是他在讲什么轶事或故事。

sentences.en: It was a memory that he seemed to be reliving so painfully in real time in front of us while he sat at the table.
sentences.zh: 这是一个记忆，他坐在餐桌旁，仿佛正在我们眼前实时而痛苦地重新经历这一切。

sentences.en: I remember, after having this conversation, I remember being just mystified.
sentences.zh: 我记得，在进行完这次谈话后，我感到了深深的迷惑。

sentences.en: He seemed to have lost so much of his memory about his life.
sentences.zh: 他似乎已经失去了人生中绝大部分的记忆。

sentences.en: And yet this one thing, it was perfect, like a bell jar.
sentences.zh: 然而唯独这件事，完美无缺，就像一个密封的玻璃罐。

sentences.en: It was, like, perfectly preserved.
sentences.zh: 就好像，被完美地保存了下来。

sentences.en: And a lot of time would pass before I found out why that was.
sentences.zh: 过了很久很久，我才知道这是为什么。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: So, Ellen, it sounds like your father basically was reliving a memory of losing this canary when he was six years old.
sentences.zh: 所以，艾伦，听上去你父亲基本上是在重新经历他六岁时弄丢那只金丝雀的记忆。

sentences.en: This is a story you had never heard before.
sentences.zh: 这是你以前从没听过的一个故事。

sentences.en: What did you learn, eventually, about this memory that had seemingly resurfaced?
sentences.zh: 关于这段似乎突然重现的记忆，你后来了解到了什么？

sentences.en: My dad died, and about a year later, I was covering my beat, which is mental health.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸去世大约一年后，我正在负责我跑的口子，也就是心理健康领域。

sentences.en: And I opened my email and saw this press release come through.
sentences.zh: 我打开邮箱，看到了发来的一则新闻稿。

sentences.en: And this is pretty normal for me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说很平常。

sentences.en: I just scan them to see whether it's something that we should cover.
sentences.zh: 我只是快速浏览一下，看看有没有什么值得我们报道的题材。

sentences.en: But this particular press release really caught my attention.
sentences.zh: 但特别巧的是，这则新闻稿真的吸引了我的注意。

sentences.en: It was for a paper in Nature Neuroscience about the creation of memory.
sentences.zh: 那是关于《自然·神经科学》杂志上一篇关于记忆生成的论文的。

sentences.en: And almost immediately, it made me think of that whole thing that we had been trying to manage with my father during those years.
sentences.zh: 几乎立刻，它就让我想起了那些年里我们一直试图应对我父亲的种种状况。

sentences.en: So I reached out to the scientist who had written the paper, Priya Rajasethopathy.
sentences.zh: 于是我联系了这篇论文的作者，普莉亚·拉贾塞托帕蒂。

sentences.en: And we talked about her work.
sentences.zh: 我们聊了聊她的研究。

sentences.en: I interviewed her.
sentences.zh: 我采访了她。

sentences.en: And at the end of the conversation, I told her about my father, that he had a fall, that after the fall, his memories were scrambled,
sentences.zh: 在对话快结束时，我跟她讲了我父亲的事：他摔过一跤，摔跤之后，他的记忆就错乱了，

sentences.en: and that some of them seemed to bob to the surface in a way I couldn't understand.
sentences.zh: 其中有些记忆似乎以一种我无法理解的方式浮出水面。

sentences.en: And she asked me if I had any scans of his brain.
sentences.zh: 她问我有没有他大脑的扫描图。

sentences.en: And presumably, you did from his time being ill.
sentences.zh: 按理说，他生病期间你应该是有的。

sentences.en: We didn't.
sentences.zh: 我们没有。

sentences.en: But I began what would turn out to be kind of a prolonged process of getting a hold of the scans that were taken right after his fall.
sentences.zh: 但我开始了一段漫长得可以说是旷日持久的过程，去设法获取他摔跤后立刻拍下的扫描图。

sentences.en: So that you could show them to her.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以拿去给她看了。

sentences.en: So I could show them to her.
sentences.zh: 这样我就可以拿去给她看。

sentences.en: So what did she make of them when she saw them?
sentences.zh: 那她看到这些扫描图时有什么看法？

sentences.en: Well, we arranged to meet in her office at Rockefeller University, which is this beautiful old campus overlooking the East River.
sentences.zh: 我们约好在洛克菲勒大学她的办公室见面，那是座俯瞰东河的漂亮老校园。

sentences.en: And I was very excited to have finally shown up with these scans.
sentences.zh: 我当时非常兴奋，终于带着这些扫描图赶到了。

sentences.en: But she wasn't able to open them.
sentences.zh: 但她打不开。

sentences.en: She didn't have the software.
sentences.zh: 她没有相应的软件。

sentences.en: So I ended up walking away empty-handed.
sentences.zh: 结果我只好空手而归。

sentences.en: But a day or two later, she sent me a text message.
sentences.zh: 但就在一两天后，她给我发了一条短信。

sentences.en: And she said, I've been able to open them.
sentences.zh: 她说，我能打开了。

sentences.en: There's something pretty interesting.
sentences.zh: 有个挺有意思的发现。

sentences.en: And I remember getting this.
sentences.zh: 我记得收到这条消息的时候。

sentences.en: I think I was in the office working on something else.
sentences.zh: 我想我当时正在办公室忙别的事情。

sentences.en: And just teared up because I couldn't believe that there was something to find in the scans.
sentences.zh: 然后眼泪就夺眶而出了，因为我不敢相信扫描图里真的能发现什么线索。

sentences.en: And she told me to come back the next day.
sentences.zh: 她让我第二天再去一趟。

sentences.en: And that's what I did.
sentences.zh: 于是我就去了。

sentences.en: And when you went back, what did she tell you?
sentences.zh: 当你再次过去时，她跟你说了什么？

sentences.en: So.
sentences.zh: 那么。

sentences.en: I mean, do you look at the brains of people you know?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你们会去看自己认识的人的大脑吗？

sentences.en: I have to assume not.
sentences.zh: 我猜不会吧。

sentences.en: No, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实不会。

sentences.en: I sat down.
sentences.zh: 我坐了下来。

sentences.en: And right away.
sentences.zh: 马上就开始了。

sentences.en: And then here's the CT scan.
sentences.zh: 接着，这就是CT扫描图。

sentences.en: She was showing me cross-sections of my father's brain.
sentences.zh: 她正在向我展示我父亲大脑的横截面。

sentences.en: See this?
sentences.zh: 看到这个了吗？

sentences.en: Where?
sentences.zh: 哪儿？

sentences.en: There.
sentences.zh: 这儿。

sentences.en: This white thing?
sentences.zh: 这个白色的东西？

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: This is, I'll show you a different view of it.
sentences.zh: 这是……我给你看个不同的视角。

sentences.en: This is kind of the biggest bleed that he has.
sentences.zh: 这是他脑中最大的一处出血点。

sentences.en: And she pointed out to me what looked like a star or like a burst of white, which was deep in the brain.
sentences.zh: 她向我指出那个看起来像星星或一团白色闪光的东西，它位于大脑深处。

sentences.en: Boom.
sentences.zh: 轰。

sentences.en: There it is.
sentences.zh: 就在那儿。

sentences.en: Yeah, there it is.
sentences.zh: 对，就在那儿。

sentences.en: And what was she pointing to exactly?
sentences.zh: 她具体指着的是什么？

sentences.en: What was she seeing?
sentences.zh: 她看到了什么？

sentences.en: What she had seen was the bleed that damaged his brain after he fell.
sentences.zh: 她看到的是他摔倒后损伤大脑的出血点。

sentences.en: All from the fall.
sentences.zh: 全都是摔倒造成的。

sentences.en: These are immediate.
sentences.zh: 这些都是即时形成的。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: The white bleeds are immediate.
sentences.zh: 白色的出血点是即时产生的。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: The brain bleed had directly affected the hippocampus,
sentences.zh: 脑出血直接影响了海马体，

sentences.en: which is this part of the brain that's known to be the kind of engine of memory that kind of takes in stimulus from the outside world, differentiates,
sentences.zh: 也就是大脑中那个被称为记忆引擎的部分，它负责接收外界的刺激，进行区分，

sentences.en: and records important stimulus as something that is going to be retained as a memory.
sentences.zh: 并把重要的刺激记录为将被当作记忆保留的东西。

sentences.en: For instance, here's the hippocampus on the other side.
sentences.zh: 比如，这是另一侧的海马体。

sentences.en: You see this, uh...
sentences.zh: 你看这个，呃……

sentences.en: Yeah, looks like a seahorse.
sentences.zh: 对，看起来像个海马。

sentences.en: Like a seahorse.
sentences.zh: 就像海马一样。

sentences.en: And you see it on this side, and that's kind of where the bleed is.
sentences.zh: 你在这一侧也能看到，出血点差不多就在这里。

sentences.en: It's only on the right side.
sentences.zh: 它只在右侧。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: So, his injury was on the right hippocampus, which is the part of the brain that organizes your sense of place and location.
sentences.zh: 所以，他的损伤在右侧海马体，这是大脑中负责组织空间感和方位感的区域。

sentences.en: And, of course, that is exactly what we have been struggling with for four years.
sentences.zh: 当然，这正是我们四年来一直在苦苦挣扎的问题。

sentences.en: For sure, what the picture shows and what I experienced lines up, that, like, that the thing that he couldn't do is, like, we couldn't convince him that he was in the right house.
sentences.zh: 确实，图片显示的和我经历的完全吻合，他做不到的事情，比如，我们无法让他相信他在自己家里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, this is, like, the first time, it sounds like, that you were really being given an explanation for what you've experienced with your father when he was disoriented,
sentences.zh: 所以，听起来这好像是第一次，有人真正为你父亲神志不清时的经历提供了一个解释，

sentences.en: when he felt like he was not in the right place, when he was restless, when he was trying to leave.
sentences.zh: 当他觉得自己不在正确的地方时，当他感到焦躁不安时，当他试图离开时。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was like a physiological, concrete explanation.
sentences.zh: 是的，就像是一个生理上的、具体的解释。

sentences.en: Okay, so the hippocampus is damaged, but how does that help explain the canary story, like the older memories that seem to be undamaged?
sentences.zh: 好的，所以海马体受损了，但这怎么能解释金丝雀的故事呢？比如那些看起来没有受损的更早的记忆？

sentences.en: So, she told me that there are some memories that can be stored in more protected parts of the brain, like the prefrontal cortex, so that they stick around,
sentences.zh: 所以，她告诉我，有些记忆可以储存在大脑中受保护更多的部分，比如前额叶皮层，这样它们就能留存下来，

sentences.en: even if the hippocampus is really damaged.
sentences.zh: 即使海马体真的严重受损。

sentences.en: So, why are some memories stored in one place and saved, and other memories are stored in another place and lost?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么有些记忆储存在一个地方并被保存下来，而另一些记忆储存在另一个地方却丢失了呢？

sentences.en: What you've taught me about the thalamus is the role that it plays in gating.
sentences.zh: 你教给我的关于丘脑的知识，是它在门控中所起的作用。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, what she has discovered is that there's an organ in the brain called the thalamus that seems to function as a gatekeeper.
sentences.zh: 所以，她发现大脑中有一个叫丘脑的器官，它的功能似乎就像一个看门人。

sentences.en: Our brains naturally say what's important.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑自然会分清什么是重要的。

sentences.en: The canary's important.
sentences.zh: 金丝雀很重要。

sentences.en: You know, meeting my wife was important.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，遇见我妻子很重要。

sentences.en: And the thalamus gates it and transferred it to the cortex.
sentences.zh: 而丘脑对它进行门控并将其转移到皮层。

sentences.en: That sends these particularly salient memories, particularly important memories, into the more protected parts of the brain.
sentences.zh: 它将这些特别显眼的记忆、特别重要的记忆，发送到大脑受保护更多的区域。

sentences.en: And that's why he had these cortical memories that really were still so important to him.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他会有这些对她而言依然如此重要的皮层记忆。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And how does the thalamus decide what goes where?
sentences.zh: 那么丘脑是如何决定什么去哪里的呢？

sentences.en: Well, that's what she's trying to figure out.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这正是她一直在试图弄清楚的。

sentences.en: Like, the canary is a kind of traumatic memory.
sentences.zh: 比如，金丝雀是一种创伤性记忆。

sentences.en: Other memories, like Tonawanda, like, that was like a rewarding memory.
sentences.zh: 其他的记忆，比如托纳旺达，那是一种有回报的记忆。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But are you saying, like, we keep both of them?
sentences.zh: 但你是说，我们把这两者都保留了吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She thinks that it has to do with what she called valence, the kind of intensity of the experience, whether it's negative or positive.
sentences.zh: 她认为这与她所说的效价有关，也就是体验的强度，无论是消极的还是积极的。

sentences.en: It can be really good or really bad.
sentences.zh: 它可以非常好，也可以非常糟。

sentences.en: But if it's high on the valence spectrum of both, we can see them selected at the level of the thalamus.
sentences.zh: 但如果两者都在效价谱的高端，我们就能看到它们在丘脑层面被筛选出来。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And so we have active projects going on in terms of how that's happening, but we don't know yet how it assigns that value.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正在进行积极的项目来研究这是如何发生的，但我们还不知道它是如何分配这种价值的。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: But it's very clear that it does.
sentences.zh: 但很明显它确实这样做了。

sentences.en: And I think that happens actually.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这确实发生了。

sentences.en: So, like, the canary story, for instance, might have stayed, perhaps, because it was something that really meant a lot to your father, really impacted him at a young age,
sentences.zh: 所以，比如金丝雀的故事，之所以留存下来，也许是因为它对你父亲意义重大，在他很小的时候就深深影响了他，

sentences.en: theoretically?
sentences.zh: 理论上是这样吗？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: What are the implications of all of this, her research, what she's learning?
sentences.zh: 所有这一切——她的研究、她所了解到的东西，意味着什么？

sentences.en: I think it raises this sort of tantalizing possibility that maybe we could help people hold on to some memories that are just really essential to living.
sentences.zh: 我认为这提出了一个极其诱人的可能性，也许我们可以帮助人们留住一些对生活至关重要的记忆。

sentences.en: If you look at early-stage Alzheimer's, they often come in and they still have some functioning.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看阿尔茨海默病早期阶段的患者，他们来看病时通常还保留着一些功能。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: If you could somehow learn to manipulate that gatekeeping mechanism, what's happening in the thalamus.
sentences.zh: 如果你能以某种方式学会操纵这种门控机制，即丘脑中发生的事情。

sentences.en: If you can go in and say, hey, there are weak things that are coming in, they're not able to be stabilized by the hippocampus itself, but if we can offload them very quickly,
sentences.zh: 如果你能介入并说，嘿，有一些微弱的信息进来了，它们无法被海马体本身稳定下来，但如果我们能非常迅速地卸载它们，

sentences.en: can we send them off?
sentences.zh: 我们能把它们发送出去吗？

sentences.en: You could move those memories out of the damaged parts of the brain into healthier long-term storage before they're loSt.
sentences.zh: 你可以把这些记忆在丢失之前，从大脑受损的区域转移到更健康的长期存储区中。

sentences.en: Even if half of it's gone or 80% of it's gone, if 20%, 10% of our neurons are okay,
sentences.zh: 即使一半没了，或者百分之八十没了，只要百分之二十、百分之十的神经元还正常，

sentences.en: and we're right there offloading things and stimulating this part of the brain to get things into the circuit, I think of that as a promising approach.
sentences.zh: 我们就在那里卸载信息并刺激大脑的这部分区域让信息进入回路，我认为这是一种很有前景的方法。

sentences.en: Does it feel to you like this is moving faster than it ever has, like our understanding is?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这比以往任何时候都发展得更快吗，比如我们的理解力？

sentences.en: For me, it just feels like it's real and new.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，我只觉得这一切既真实又崭新。

sentences.en: Those are the two things I feel most about.
sentences.zh: 这是我感触最深的两个方面。

sentences.en: You mentioned the idea of saving memories that are essential.
sentences.zh: 你提到了保存至关重要记忆的想法。

sentences.en: What memories are we talking about specifically?
sentences.zh: 我们具体在谈论哪些记忆？

sentences.en: I mean, recognizing your family, the people around you, recognizing the place where you are, and knowing that you're home or that you're safe.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，认出你的家人、周围的人，认出你所在的地方，知道你在家或者你是安全的。

sentences.en: The kinds of things that, at the end of your life, you really want to hold on to.
sentences.zh: 那些在生命尽头，你真的很想紧紧抓住的东西。

sentences.en: How did it feel, Ellen, to walk away from that meeting with at least some kind of theory about what your father had experienced at the end of his life?
sentences.zh: 艾伦，带着对你父亲在生命尽头所经历的事情的某种理论离开那次会面，感觉如何？

sentences.en: So I remember walking away from that meeting really sort of thrilled.
sentences.zh: 所以我记得离开那次会面时真的非常激动。

sentences.en: It was so surprising that there was something so physiological that could kind of explain what we had been through during that time.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，竟然有如此生理层面的东西可以解释我们在那段时期经历的一切。

sentences.en: And I remember calling my husband and telling him the part of his brain that was injured in the fall, that was the part that creates memories about location and place.
sentences.zh: 我记得我打电话给我丈夫，告诉他我父亲跌倒时受伤的大脑部位，正是那个产生位置和地点记忆的部位。

sentences.en: It just, it explains so much.
sentences.zh: 这简直，这解释了太多事情。

sentences.en: And I asked, what are you thinking?
sentences.zh: 我问，你在想什么？

sentences.en: And he just, he said it made him feel sad.
sentences.zh: 他只是，他说这让他感到难过。

sentences.en: Wait, why did he feel sad?
sentences.zh: 等等，他为什么会觉得难过？

sentences.en: Well, to understand this, you'd have to sort of understand the way our household functioned.
sentences.zh: 嗯，要理解这一点，你得了解我们家庭的运作方式。

sentences.en: And I was working a lot, I was traveling a lot, and my husband was the one who, more often than not, had to track down my dad when he wandered away.
sentences.zh: 我当时工作很忙，经常出差，而我丈夫才是那个常常不得不去寻找迷路的父亲的人。

sentences.en: Had to find him on the side of the road, in our neighborhood, talk him into getting in the car, tell him some kind of story about why he had to go home.
sentences.zh: 得在路边、在我们社区找到他，劝说他上车，编造各种理由告诉他为什么要回家。

sentences.en: He's the one that took him to the airport, and I think he just felt sad that for all this time, we didn't really understand that there was a permanent change,
sentences.zh: 他是带他去机场的人，我想他只是觉得难过，这么长时间以来，我们并不知道这是一个永久性的改变，

sentences.en: that something had changed about him, that we couldn't talk him out of it.
sentences.zh: 他身上发生了某种变化，我们无法说服他改变看法。

sentences.en: We couldn't retrain him or teach him.
sentences.zh: 我们无法重新训练他或教导他。

sentences.en: You couldn't reason with him, convince him where his home was.
sentences.zh: 你无法跟他讲道理，无法让他相信他的家在哪里。

sentences.en: But also that, like, no one had told us, you know, you're going to spend the rest of his life trying to persuade him that he's home.
sentences.zh: 而且也没有人告诉过我们，你知道的，你将用他余下的生命去试图说服他他已经到家了。

sentences.en: Do you think if you had known any of this, it would have changed how you interacted with him?
sentences.zh: 你觉得如果你早知道这些，会改变你与他互动的方式吗？

sentences.en: I think it would have helped to know that we couldn't talk him out of it.
sentences.zh: 我想如果知道我们无法说服他，会很有帮助。

sentences.en: It would have helped to know, like, this is a one-way change.
sentences.zh: 如果知道这是一个不可逆转的变化，会很有帮助。

sentences.en: It's not changing back.
sentences.zh: 它不会变回去了。

sentences.en: It would have helped to know he wasn't being stubborn or willful or impulsive, but that, you know, something had changed about his brain where he just couldn't compute.
sentences.zh: 如果知道他不是在固执、任性或冲动，而是他的大脑发生了某种变化导致他无法正常计算，这会对我们有所帮助。

sentences.en: I think it would have helped us come to peace with the fact that he was a different person from before the fall.
sentences.zh: 我想这会帮助我们接受这样一个事实：他已经不再是跌倒前的那个不同的人了。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Understanding what's happening in the brain doesn't mean that you can stop it or reverse it, but it may prepare you better for accompanying them to the end.
sentences.zh: 理解大脑中发生的事情并不意味着你能阻止它或逆转它，但它可能会让你更好地陪伴他们走到最后。

sentences.en: Ellen, thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 艾伦，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由卢克·范德普洛格（Luke Vander Ploeg）制作，亚历克斯·巴伦（Alex Barron）和蒂娜·安托利尼（Tina Antolini）提供了帮助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Wendy Doerr and engineered by Rowan Nemisto.
sentences.zh: 温迪·多尔（Wendy Doerr）剪辑，罗文·内米斯托（Rowan Nemisto）混音。

sentences.en: Production assistance and fact-checking by Dahlia Haddad.
sentences.zh: 达莉亚·哈达德（Dahlia Haddad）负责制作协助和事实核查。

sentences.en: And contains music by Marian Lozano and Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: 节目中包含玛丽安·洛萨诺（Marian Lozano）和丹·鲍威尔（Dan Powell）的音乐。

sentences.en: That's it for the Sunday Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期“周日日报”的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Rachel AbraMs.
sentences.zh: 我是蕾切尔·亚伯拉罕斯（Rachel Abrams）。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《切割机秀》将为您准备假期接待客人的相关内容。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 请收听关于如何让您的客人在家中感到宾至如归的实用技巧。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种对光线极度敏感、必须全黑才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会不会晕厥过去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线环境？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症吗，对食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶的人？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 请在《纽约时报》应用程序或您喜欢收听播客的任何地方搜索收听《切割机秀》。
